column15: Confirmed real: Distillerie de Bercloux, founded 2002 by Philippe Laclie in the Cognac region of Charente-Maritime, France (16 Rue de la Mairie, Bercloux) -- began offering Single Malt Bercloux in 2016, confirmed via the distillery's own site (bercloux.fr) and a whisky retailer's history page. Corrected kind from blend to distillery (a real, named, operating French distillery, not an undisclosed-origin label). Third-party sources describe "future" peated/smoked whiskies as merely planned circa 2018; no producer-domain confirmation that a peated release exists today, so kept unknown rather than asserted.

Confirmed via Heaven Hill's own product page (corrected the seed's unrelated Irish-whiskey Wikipedia link): Bernheim Original is a 7-year-old Kentucky Straight Wheat Whiskey made at Heaven Hill's Bernheim plant in Louisville -- "the first new style of American whiskey since Prohibition." defaultTypeName stays empty (wheat whiskey has no match in the closed list). peatProfile=none: no peat/smoke on the producer's own page; American-whiskey convention (not a positive claim, so no domain corroboration required).

Confirmed via the brand's own site (bibandtuckerbourbon.com): small-batch bourbon aged a minimum of 6 years in Tennessee, corn/rye/barley mash bill, matching the sample "Bib&Tucker Small Batch." Owner corrected via oakr.com's deep-dive: Deutsch Family Wine & Spirits owns it as a non-distiller producer sourcing Tennessee bourbon (widely attributed to Cascade Hollow/George Dickel, though officially undisclosed, so no distillery asserted). Kind corrected from blend to brand. peatProfile=none, no peat/smoke on the producer's own page; American-bourbon convention.

Corrected: real cowboy-themed brand with its own site (billy-bong.com), owned by Les Producteurs Réunis (French spirits company) per their own product listing, which states the Straight Bourbon's origin as "US." The brand also carries a separate "Billy Bong American Whiskey" line, so defaultTypeName is left empty (spans more than one type) rather than the seed's "bourbon". Kind corrected from distillery to brand (no distillery of its own; sourced/bottled for the brand owner). peatProfile=none: no peat/smoke mentioned anywhere; American-whiskey convention.

Resolved (the seed correctly spotted the Speyside/Glenlivet-area toponymy but stopped short of the producer): "Blairfindy" is Blackadder's substitute name for single malt Glenfarclas -- confirmed via wordsofwhisky.com (opened this session): "Glenfarclas isn't too keen on independent bottlers using their name...Blairfindy is what Blackadder settled on," corroborated by whiskybase's own brand summary and multiple auction listings titled "Glenfarclas 'Blairfindy'." parentSlug set to the already-live glenfarclas. bottlerSlug set to a new row, blackadder (Blackadder International Ltd, family-run independent bottler of single malt Scotch, est. 1995, whose signature "Raw Cask" series matches this batch's sample name exactly -- confirmed via the bottler's own site and Wikipedia). Corrected kind to brand and defaultTypeName to single malt (sources consistently call it single malt, not a blended-malt teaspoon). peatProfile=none per Glenfarclas's well-documented unpeated Speyside sherry-cask house style (also consistent with a whiskybase reviewer's comment that this bottling "destroys peaty whisky").

Upgraded from the seed's guesswork: confirmed via the bottle designer's own case-study page (thinkboldstudio.com, opened this session) that Bold Thady Irish Whiskey is a real commercial product, "a blend of the finest grain and malt," triple distilled and married in first-fill bourbon casks -- matches the sample "Bold Thady Bourbon Casks Matured" exactly. Name-origin guess (the folk song "Bold Thady Quill") is confirmed on the same page. No specific distillery/bottler company identified. peatProfile=none, no peat/smoke in the recipe description; ordinary Irish blend.

Confirmed via Michter's own product page: Bomberger's Declaration is a genuine Michter's Legacy Series release (108-proof Kentucky Straight Bourbon, aged in Chinquapin and Hungarian oak), validating the seed's parentSlug=michters (already live). Note for a reviewer: Wikipedia's Bomberger's Distillery article separately describes an unrelated modern "Bomberger's"-branded blend from Heritage Spirits/Thistle Finch Distillery (Lancaster, PA) that is NOT this product -- two different companies revived the name independently. peatProfile=none, no peat/smoke on Michter's own page; American-bourbon convention.

Confirmed (the seed's "believed, not confirmed" is now settled): Bonailie Blended Malt Scotch Whisky is "produced by the team at the Bladnoch distillery in the Lowlands" (caskcartel.com, opened this session, cross-checked against a Master of Malt snippet naming Bladnoch too). parentSlug set to the already-live bladnoch. Corrected kind to brand and defaultTypeName to malt (blended malt specifically, not the seed's generic "blend"). "Bonailie" is Scottish Gaelic for a parting drink. peatProfile=none, no peat/smoke mentioned; matches Lowland's characteristically light, unpeated style.

Re-verified this session (opened Wikipedia directly): "Buchanan's is a brand of Scotch whisky produced by Diageo in Scotland," established 1884 by James Buchanan & Co. Matches the seed exactly; confidence raised from low to high since the citation is now personally confirmed. peatProfile=none, no peat or smoke character mentioned.

Confirmed via the bottler's own site (adrattray.com, opened this session): Cask Orkney 15 Year Old is "a lightly peated single malt, capturing the spirit of Orkney" from A.D. Rattray's Casks of Scotland collection -- source distillery deliberately undisclosed (parentSlug left blank), matching the Secret Orkney pattern (Orkney has only two distilleries, Highland Park and Scapa; Scapa releases no independent bottlings). peatProfile=light satisfies the gate via direct bottler-domain corroboration. bottlerSlug set to the already-live dewar-rattray: A.D. Rattray's own "Our Story" page confirms the company was founded by Andrew Dewar Rattray in 1868, run today by the Morrison family -- the same entity as "A Dewar Rattray." Corrected kind to brand.

Identified via the producer's own site (twojames.com): Catcher's Rye Whiskey is made in-house by Two James Spirits, Corktown, Detroit, Michigan ("the first legal distillery in Detroit since Prohibition" per The Whiskey Wash, cross-checked, and consistent with Whiskybase's brand entry dated 2016) -- 100% Michigan rye mash, no barley. Corrected kind from blend to brand and set owner. Flag for reviewer: a separate, internally-inconsistent article (glassandnote.com) describes an unrelated "Catcher's Rye" story (Michter's-contracted, Pennsylvania, "Catcher's Spirits LLC," 2021 launch) that contradicts every other source checked, including the producer's own page -- disregarded as unreliable. peatProfile=none, no peat/smoke on the producer's page; American-rye convention.

Corrected substantially: NOT Irish whiskey (the seed's assumption from the "Celtic" name was wrong). Celtic Revival is a 12-year-old Single Malt SCOTCH Whisky from Linkwood Distillery (Speyside, already live), bottled by Brave New Spirits (Glasgow-based independent bottler, new bottlerSlug row added, see below) -- confirmed via the bottler's own site (bravenewspirits.com, opened this session), which also lists an IWSC 2023 Silver Award. No peat/smoke mentioned; matches Linkwood's well-known light, floral, unpeated Speyside house style.

Cross-verified this session: Civitas whisky ("produced in Moldova using an original Scottish technology," barley malt) is a product of Chateau Cojușna (alcomarket.md, opened), a real Moldovan winery near Chișinău founded 1995 (confirmed on the winery's own site, cojusna.com, though whisky is not mentioned on its front page -- wine/brandy/grappa are its stated focus). Corrected kind from distillery to brand (a diversified winery's product line, not a dedicated whisky distillery). Range spans a classic and flavored Honey/Apple variants, so defaultTypeName stays empty. peatProfile=unknown, no mention anywhere; not a well-established category with a safe default.

Corrected/confirmed via the producer's own site (craterlakespirits.com/whiskey, opened this session): Crater Lake Rye Whiskey, made by Hood River Distillers, Inc., Oregon -- 100% rye mash bill, matching the sample name exactly. (Secondary sources associate the brand's origin with Bendistillery, Bend OR, not contradicted but not stated on the producer's current page -- flagging for a reviewer in case the two are organizationally distinct.) countryCode/defaultTypeName corrected from the seed's name-based inference to directly verified facts. peatProfile=none, no peat/smoke mentioned; American-rye convention.

Confirmed real, internationally distributed (Ukraine, Poland, Germany, Kazakhstan, Vietnam, Hong Kong retail listings) own-label Blended Scotch Whisky, matured a minimum of 3 years -- verified via universalfws.com's own product listing (opened this session), matching the seed's characterization. No single bottling company/distillery identified despite multiple searches (Whiskybase carries reviews under "Brand: Cromwell's" but names no producer). withheld peat proposal: several independent retail listings (universalfws.com, rozetka.com.ua) describe "smoky and malty notes" in the aroma, but none is the producer's own domain, so kept unknown rather than asserted.

Producer identified via Global Spirits' own product page (globalspirits.com, opened this session): Cumberland Falls is "Authentic Kentucky Straight Bourbon," Owensboro, Kentucky, "the original distillery that opened its doors in 1885," handcrafted small-batch, 86 proof. Named for the Kentucky waterfall, as the seed guessed. (Secondary, unconfirmed sources describe this as the historic Green River Distilling Co./Owensboro Distillery site, now under Bardstown Bourbon Company -- not independently verified this session; flagging for a reviewer.) Corrected kind from distillery to brand and filled countryCode/owner. peatProfile=none, no peat/smoke mentioned; American-bourbon convention.

Producer identified via the brand's own site (daddyrack.com, opened this session): "Bottled by Daddy Rack Whiskey Co., Columbia, Tennessee, USA," created by Master Maker & Blender J. Arthur Rackham ("Daddy Rack"). Confirms Tennessee Straight Whiskey (matches the sample and the seed's defaultTypeName) and the Lincoln County Process (maple-charcoal filtering) -- charcoal mellowing is not peat. Corrected kind from blend to brand and filled owner. peatProfile=none, no peat/smoke mentioned; American-whiskey convention.

Corrected countryCode from XX to FR: Deep River Single Malt is a French own-label whisky by Les Grands Chais de France (a large French wine/spirits group -- note the parallel with "Billy Bong" elsewhere in this batch, a different French group's own-label bourbon). Confirmed via a Ukrainian retailer's product page (alcomag.ua, opened this session) naming the brand owner and French origin explicitly; a WIPO trademark-database snippet (seen, not independently re-opened) separately names "LES GRANDS CHAIS DE FRANCE S.A.S." as the DEEP RIVER trademark holder, corroborating. Corrected kind from blend to brand. withheld peat proposal: the retailer's tasting notes describe "strong fenolic [sic] and smoky notes" and a "smoky, salty" aroma with "smoke in the finish" -- phenolic character is the chemical signature of peat, strongly suggestive of a peated malt, but the source is a retailer, not the producer's own domain, so kept unknown per the brief's rule rather than asserted.

Resolved: the seed's disconnect between the catalogue brand string "Dilmoor" and the sole sample name "Gold Mill" is because the full product name is "Dilmoor Gold Mill Blended Scotch Whisky" -- confirmed via winebutik.com.ua's own listing (opened this session, states origin "Шотландія"/Scotland directly). Dilmoor itself is an Italian private-label bottler (Pedrengo, Bergamo, Italy, producing liqueurs/distillates/private label since 1950, per dilmoor.com) that also bottles an unrelated "O'Connell's Irish" whiskey and a separate "Crema Whisky Goldmill" cream liqueur under similar names, neither of which is this row's sample. countryCode set to GB-SCT (the whisky's legal origin) rather than Italy (the bottling company's home), matching this project's precedent for "Restless Pony" (Ukrainian owner, US-origin whiskey). New alias added: "gold mill" (see alias.tsv). peatProfile=none: "mild flavor with malt notes and subtle vanilla" (artdrink.com.ua), no smoke or peat mentioned; ordinary blended Scotch.

Confirmed via the brand's own official site (thedramwhisky.com, opened this session): Dram Loch is a genuine 3-Year Blended Scotch Whisky, "produced, distilled and blended in Scotland" -- built explicitly as an export/private-label brand "for distributors looking for a brand that can grow." Producing company/distillery deliberately undisclosed on the site; only a generic "Highlands" reference appears, not specific enough to assert a region. No peat/smoke mentioned; ordinary blended Scotch per the site's own description.

Confirmed via the distillery's own site (dryflydistilling.com, opened this session): located at 1021 W. Riverside, Spokane, WA. Makes multiple whiskey styles -- wheat (matches this row's "Dry Fly Cask Strength Wheat" sample), Straight Rye, and a "single pot still...small batch, single barrel whiskey inspired by the Celtic tradition" -- so defaultTypeName is kept empty (multi-type range; corrected reasoning from the seed's "not one of the 8 listed values" framing to "spans several of the 8 listed values"). No peat/smoke mentioned; American craft-whiskey convention.

Confirmed via the producer's own site (dwdwhiskey.com/whiskey.php, opened this session): Dublin's Own is made by DWD (Dublin Whiskey Distillery) -- "an outstanding blend of single malt and grain," double and triple distilled. Matches the seed's inference exactly (Irish own-label blend), now evidenced rather than assumed. peatProfile=none: no peat/smoke in the producer's own tasting notes (honey, vanilla, caramel, chocolate, spice).

New row for blairfindy. Independent bottler of single malt Scotch whisky, family-run, founded 1995 by Robin Tucek and John Lamond (named after the historic Bishop John Blackadder); signature range is "Raw Cask" (cask-strength, unfiltered, containing cask sediment). Confirmed via the bottler's own site and Wikipedia. No single house style or peat default (bottles casks from many distilleries).

New row for celtic-revival. Glasgow-based independent bottler ("331 Charles Street, Glasgow G21 2QA"), releasing single-cask and branded ranges (Celtic Revival, Cask Masters, WhiskyHeroes) sourced from multiple distilleries and regions -- no single peat or type default. Confirmed via the bottler's own site. (Note for the merge process: batch 07's own output independently added the same slug for "spirit-of-voodoo," describing the same bottler consistently.)
